accuracy.evidence: Definitions and methods checked against the AQA GCSE Statistics 8382 specification (sampling: simple random, systematic, stratified, with proportional allocation), the Edexcel GCSE Statistics 1ST0 specification, CCSS 7.SP.1, and Moore, McCabe and Craig, Introduction to the Practice of Statistics (simple random sample: every set of n equally likely; systematic sampling with a periodic frame). Every lab number was recomputed: 60 ÷ 6 = 10; 240, 200, 160, 200 of 800 give 12, 10, 8, 10 of 40; 360 of 600 gives 30 of 50; 200 ÷ 8 = 25. The adult text states that systematic sampling is not a simple random sample, which is the precise distinction.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented errors from GCSE examiner reports: substituting a nearby number for one out of range (step 1 prediction and the 58 feedback, p3), keeping repeats (step 1 07, challenge 'twice', m4), wrong interval using n or N (step 2 k = 6 and 12 feedback, challenge 'kn'/'kN', m1), always starting at 1 (m6), periodic bias in systematic sampling (step 3 prediction, p4), equal rather than proportional strata (step 4 prediction and the all-10 feedback, challenge 'equal', m5), and calling convenience samples random (challenge 'handy', p5), plus the belief that a random sample matches the population exactly (challenge 'exact', m9).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagrsamp is about the selection procedures themselves: accept or skip decisions on a random number table against a numbered frame, an interval and random-start picker that highlights every kth cell, a street with a period-10 pattern that exposes systematic bias, steppers for proportional strata with a live total, and a three-way method sort. flagsample (ages 12–14) is population versus sample, convenience bias and sample size; it has no table, interval, period or strata. Gate similarity is under 30% to every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds each rule by acting: using 58 is refused because no such student exists and substitution gives extra chances; k = 6 is refused because it gives 10 people; start 10 on the street picks all four corner houses, and start 3 picks none, so the bias is seen not told; setting every year to 10 triggers the proportion feedback; and each method card is refused with the defining feature of the right method.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options: use student 50 for 58 (step 1, disproved when the lab rejects substitution), a systematic sample is automatically fair (step 3, disproved by the all-corner-houses start), and 10 from each year is fair (step 4, disproved by the proportional 12, 10, 8, 10). The reveal after each task confirms the right option.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Ten distinct wrong-answer messages: equal (halves ignore size), tenth (took a tenth of 360), exact (random does not mean exact match), quick (random is about fairness, not speed), kn and kN (wrong interval formula), twice (repeat counted), stop (stopping at a repeat), handy (opportunity sample), luck (only stratifying guarantees the mix). Six questions rotate.

readability.evidence: Learner kid text measures FK 4.7 against the 6.5 target, with each method in its own paragraph and one worked example (240 ÷ 800 × 40 = 12). Adult text is FK 7.5 against 9.5 and names the precise terms sampling frame, stratum, proportional allocation and sampling interval. Lab prompts are one line each.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph defines one method or one caution; there is no introduction or summary padding. Lab messages are either the task or a reason tied to the exact number tapped (Every 6th of 60 gives 10 people, not 6). No banned phrases pass the content gate.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark for all 6 steps: the 50- and 60-cell grids are 10 columns of about 30 px cells, the random pairs fit one row, the stratified steppers sit at the right edge with bars that shrink to fit, and the method bins are three equal columns. The hidden-pattern status line was overflowing at 390 px, so it was changed to auto-shrinking chips and rechecked.

accessibility.evidence: The walkthrough gate ran every step with Show me on desktop and iPhone and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in either theme. Every canvas action has a button: Use/Skip for the current pair, k and start buttons, start 1 to 10 for the street, plus and minus per year, and the three method buttons. The canvas aria-label carries every feedback message.
